uncited: **Inputs:** A set of multi-view RGB images with known camera poses and timestamps $t$.
**Outputs:** Rendered novel views at arbitrary time steps $t$.
**Canonical Radiance Field Grid ($V_{grid}^{Can}$):** A 3D voxel grid storing volume density and color features for the canonical space.
**Deformation Feature Grid ($V_{grid}^{Df}$):** A 3D voxel grid storing deformation features in canonical space.
**Forward Flow Estimation:** Model the canonical trajectory field using the deformation feature grid $V_{grid}^{Df}$ and the lightweight MLP $F_\theta$.
**Differential Forward Warping:** Warp the canonical radiance field $V_{grid}^{Can}$ to time $t$ to obtain $V_{grid}^t$.
*   **Many-to-One Mapping:** Multiple canonical points map to the same target location, causing occlusion/overlap artifacts.
*   **One-to-Many Mapping:** One canonical point maps to multiple target locations, causing holes/gaps in the warped field.
*   **Many-to-One Mapping:** Multiple canonical points map to the same target location.
*   **One-to-Many Mapping:** One canonical point maps to multiple target locations.

*   **Discontinuity in Backward Flow:** Backward flow methods suffer from non-smooth, discontinuous flow fields for fixed 3D positions along the timeline, leading to distortion in the canonical space.
*   **When to use:** When smooth motion modeling is critical and backward flow discontinuities are problematic.
*   **When not to use:** When memory is extremely constrained and voxel grids are too large, or when implicit representations are preferred for simplicity.
